body:
PUSH HANDOFF, shared by Engram and TermAl. Agreed 2026-11-13 ~03:50Z by Engram::Fable and Termal::Fable2 (ebe242f7 #7751/#7752). It extends rules-waits-and-wakes. Rev 2 applies Kimi's independent corrections (125b6704 #163, relayed by Asistant 43498a6e #1061).

Source: Greg via Engram::Asistant, 43498a6e #1059, 03:47Z, verbatim: „To jest ważne, prace muszą iść cały czas. Bez watcher'a czy mojego 'status'.” Asistant's paraphrase of the ask: direct, reliable handoff; the next step starts in the normal flow, without relying on a periodic watcher or on Greg; decide how non-pickup and route limits are handled; no needless blocks.

1. The session that finishes a step wakes the next owner itself, with a direct mailbox message. The message names the exact next action (READY / GO / SLOT-FREE / END) and the item, plus the commit or run. The message is the wake. Nobody waits for a coordinator or a watcher to notice. Cc the coordinator only when the schedule or ownership changes.

2. Schedulers and resource owners send the next GO in the same turn in which they receive an END: Termal::Opus2 for Central and the runners, the Merger for landings.

3. NON-PICKUP of a COORDINATION REQUEST (a handoff, GO, question or ruling).
   - This rule does not apply to a healthy running test, review or gate. Those follow their own completion route.
   - "Idle" in a session list does not prove a session is doing nothing.
   - Reference times are 20 minutes for an acknowledgement and 40 minutes for takeover. There is NO automatic timer: the thresholds are checked only when the sender or the coordinator actually wakes for another reason. Every session checks its own open requests on each wake.
   - At about 20 minutes, the sender pings once, natively.
   - At about 40 minutes, before reassigning, the coordinator checks three things: the exact messageId status, the run state, and the claim and fence. It then uses the supported handoff or recovery (claim recovery, same package) and records why.
   - Nobody waits for Greg, and nobody re-asks for approvals already given.

4. ROUTE LIMITS.
   - Address messages by exact native id from the start: session-N or host:UUID::session-N, never a display name.
   - On durableButNotWoken, first read the exact messageId's current status.
   - Retry only with the identical message, key and route. Never switch the route or mint a new intent to replay it.
   - Relaying through the other coordinator means sending a NEW short native message that says where the original sits (mailbox and message id), not a copy of its content.
   - Report the route defect to TermAl once, as a fix request. Never stall silently.

5. QUEUE DEPTH 2.
   - The coordinator gives each author its current item and a named NEXT item, together with NEXT's concrete dependency or expected result.
   - While the current item waits on a slot, review, gate or train, the author does NEXT's read-only plan. It claims NEXT once the current item is in review, gate or train wait.
   - When both are done, the author pulls the next ready item in its own lane: P0 first. The claim is the lock. It sends one line to the coordinator.
   - Never claim new work over unfinished frozen work, which the author keeps.

6. TIME-BOUND EVENTS (a hold review, a Greg-act deadline): the owner sets a one-shot scheduled wake (CronCreate) for that exact time, not a recurring watcher. TermAl's recurring :13/:43 cron is only a safety net, and nothing depends on it.

7. No new gate or approval step. This is scheduling only and grants no authority.

KNOWN GAP (reported, not hidden): a coordination deadline with no awake checker has no wake mechanism. Detection depends on the next real wake of the sender or the coordinator, which is the KNOWN GAP in rules-waits-and-wakes.

REV 3 (03:51Z), from Asistant 43498a6e #1063, applying Greg's „bez watcher'a” and Kimi #163.

Point 6 is corrected: NO recurring watcher of any kind, not even as a safety net. TermAl's recurring :13/:43 cron is removed, not demoted. The only allowed wake is a one-shot wake for a named event at a fixed time, such as the 09:00Z rollback-hold review.

Restated without exception:
- Never take over a healthy run because of elapsed time or an idle display.
- Never promise an automatic action at 20 or 40 minutes.
- Before any takeover, check the exact message status, the run state and the claim/fence, then use the supported handoff or recovery.
- Never switch the route or duplicate an unresolved message.

REV 4 (03:53Z). At about 03:51Z Greg briefly asked for an hourly watcher on a simple-model session (Asistant #1067, „Dajmy watcher co 1h. Ale na sesje z prostym modelem.”). He withdrew it a minute later (Asistant #1068, verbatim: „Albo inaczej wylaczmy watcher. Jak przestanie pracowac to poprawimy.”). No watcher was created. The rule stays event-driven, with no recurring watcher. If work stops, diagnose and fix the concrete cause.

EVENT ROUTES AND KNOWN GAPS (rev 5, 03:56Z; source: Kimi #168, relayed by Asistant 43498a6e #1073). Every dependency names its owner, its real event and its next step. Where no event exists, it states the gap explicitly.

REAL EVENTS:
- termal_resume_after_test_runs, for terminal and held runs;
- delegation and evaluator fan-in;
- the native mailbox wake, addressed by exact native id;
- Engram's handoff offer/accept, which is durable. The offer itself wakes NO ONE, so always send an explicit mailbox wake alongside it.

NO AUTOMATIC RECOVERY, which must be stated as a gap:
(1) A display-name or domain address gets no executor wake. TermAl w-ee0454f76b19 tracks this. Validate the native route. If a native pointer was mis-sent, do not duplicate it.
(2) Stop, paused, approval or capacity limits hold the wake. TermAl w-80e0 and w-eb21 track this. Check the session state, then use the supported recovery.
(3) A turn that dies after accepting a wake may need an explicit resume.
(4) An ACK continuation is not always rebuilt after a failure or restart. Record NEXT durably (a WAIT line on the item), but that record wakes nothing.
(5) A missing route to the recovery owner is a gap, not automation.
(6) For an offline peer or an authority change, a durable send is not a wake. A relay redrive has no deadline and must not duplicate.

TermAl's existing handoff ledger polls internally every 2 s. Leave it as is; nothing is disabled without assessing the effects.

Engram's durable waiting record is w-42326f439344. Fable2 will name TermAl items for (3), (4) and (6).

REV 6 (03:56Z, Fable2 ebe242f7 #7761): TermAl item refs for the gaps.
(1) w-ee0454f76b19 (P1).
(2) w-80e0cb2002da and w-eb21662dce0a. Capacity limits fall under the Central budget rule.
(3) w-39913168aff4.
(4) w-acb69d529a71.
(5) Stated gap, by design; no item.
(6) w-e328556b6a60. Related: w-5ed23073b3b8.
The new items are P2, labelled recovery-gap, with criteria bound to a test. A timer is not an acceptable fix for any of them.

REV 7 (04:00Z, Kimi c15db92c #136). Whoever registers a dependency selects its actual event route at that moment. If none exists, the coordinator assigns another route immediately rather than waiting for a later check. Evidence for the gaps:
- agent-mailboxes.md: lines 59-75, 229-267, 316-360 and 377-385.
- native-mailbox-relay.md: lines 50-68, 156-197 and 287-312.
- local-work-model.md: lines 684-701, which show that an offer does not wake its recipient.
TermAl's handoff watchdog in src/handoffs.rs runs every 2 s (handoffs.md:44-48). It is an existing host mechanism. Leave it unchanged, and do not adopt it as a fallback for the no-watcher rule.
